revenue_growth_year_one.reason: The company says its demand estimates can be inaccurate, that AI clouds and model makers lack long-term contracts and investment-grade financing, and that customers may postpone new architectures for want of capital or data-center infrastructure. Receivables now run on terms up to a year, the company guarantees a customer's land, power and shell leases, and it commits to purchase cloud services from the AI clouds that procure its systems, so part of the demand is financed by the company itself. The bear case has the guided quarter land but the sequential steps after it flatten as customer capital tightens and the digestion that followed the last surge repeats; because Python fades this rate in a straight line to the terminal rate, year one is set well below what the guided quarter alone would imply for the next four quarters, so that the whole decade carries the deceleration rather than the first year only.

The base case therefore puts year one below what the immediate guide implies, so that the decade compounds at a pace a company of this size can plausibly sustain while still honoring near-term demand the company calls accelerating.
